_readme: Copy to vault/autonomyPolicy.json and edit. CAIRN never reads this file from examples/. With no policy declared the ladder is not enforced and the decision record says so — that is an absence, not a grant of autonomous execution.
_ladder: 0 OBSERVE · 1 ANALYSE · 2 RECOMMEND · 3 PREPARE · 4 EXECUTE_WITH_APPROVAL · 5 EXECUTE_AUTONOMOUSLY
_whatAnActionNeeds: A read needs ANALYSE. A write needs PREPARE. Anything that executes — including a tool CAIRN does not recognise — needs EXECUTE_WITH_APPROVAL. Levels 4 and 5 differ by exactly one thing: at 4 a person is asked, at 5 they are not.
_howRulesCombine: The LOWEST matching ceiling wins, not the most specific. Adding a rule can therefore only ever narrow what is permitted, never widen it — so a narrow permissive exception cannot silently override a broad restriction. If you want to permit more, raise the ceiling that is currently binding rather than adding an exception.
_whoARuleAppliesTo: Write user:<name> to match the operating-system username, or role:<name> to match a role declared in vault/principal.json. A bare name still works and is matched against BOTH, which is why a rule written for a role could also match a user of that name; it is reported as deprecated when you preview a policy. Use * for everyone.
_theModelHasNoSay: Levels are resolved from the action class, the protected-target class and the OS principal. None is supplied by a model, and the resolver has no parameter through which model output could arrive.
_default: Applied where no rule matches. Omit it to leave unmatched actions uncapped. Setting it to RECOMMEND is a strong posture: nothing executes anywhere without a rule explicitly permitting it.

rules.note: Nothing executes against the production trading cluster, whoever asks. CAIRN may still analyse it and recommend a change; a human carries the change out.
Nor is anything written into the production configuration root.
Unattended execution is permitted only for this service account, and only where no protected target was matched. targetClass '*' matches every action including one that touched nothing declared.
Reading is unrestricted for everyone; stated explicitly so the intent is on the record rather than inferred from the absence of a rule.
